newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks cap record week with broad-based rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks cap record week with broad-based rally.

text.p: U.S. stocks capped a record-shattering week with a fresh session of broad-based gains on Friday, inspired by a tame report on wholesale inflation.
The Dow industrials ended up unofficially 71 points, or 0.9 percent, at 7782. It was the blue chip gauge's sixth-consecutive record closing high.
For the week, the Dow ended with gains of a record 346 points, topping the index's previous biggest weekly point rise of 332 set the week ended May 2.
"It's just sort of a classic buying panic," said John Church, chief investment officer at Glenmede Trust Co.
Reflecting the rally's wide support, winning issues beat losers on the New York Stock Exchange by a two-to-one margin.
After lagging other major indexes for most of the week, the Nasdaq composite joined the record run, closing up 12 points to 1423. It eclipsed its previous all-time closing high of 1412 set Monday.
The latest catalyst for stocks to rise was a report Friday of an unexpected drop in the Producer Price Index for May, the fifth consecutive month the index has declined.
The Labor Department reported the PPI dropped 0.3 percent in May after a 0.6 percent fall in April. Economists on average had expected the May PPI to rise 0.1 percent.

The data, coupled with other recent statistics including Thursday's report on soft May retail sales, indicate little sign of inflation that could spur the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates, analysts said.
The data "is going to make it very difficult for the Fed to raise rates," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford.
With Friday's advance, the Dow has risen 477 points, or 6.5 percent, in the past six sessions.
While Wall Street stocks appear to be gathering momentum with each session, some pullback in the coming days could be in store, traders and analysts said.
They cited the sharp rise in the past days and upcoming economic data, including Tuesday's CPI report on May retail inflation, which could trigger profit taking.
"You've had a huge amount of buying power used up here in the last few days," said James Volk, director of equity trading at Jensen Securities.
Among individual stocks, American Express Co rose 3-1/2 to 76-5/8 and Citicorp added 1-5/8 to 120-5/8 on market rumors they had resumed merger talks. The two companies declined comment on the rumors.

DuPont Co gained one to 58-7/8. A Morgan Stanley analyst upgraded his rating on the stock to strong buy from outperform, citing expectations of strength in the company's pharmaceutical and agricultural products businesses.

Monsanto Co tumbled 3-1/2 to 42-3/4 after a J.P. Morgan Securities analyst cut his rating on the stock, saying its price "more than adequately reflects the company's near-term and long-term growth prospects."
Shares of Maximus Inc, a provider of program management and consulting services, rose two to 18 on their first day of trading.

Netscape Communications Corp fell 1-1/16 to 32-1/4 after saying it was investigating a potential bug found in test versions of its Internet browser. It later said it replicated the bug and planned to offer a fix early next week.
The S&P 500 index rose 9.81 points to 893.27, a record.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 11.71 points to 1423.03, a record.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
